outs.summary:
Bake v9 is built with Blender on this Mac (Cycles on the Metal GPU) and is now the default in the lane lab. At rest it matches the projected plates region by region within 2 levels. The v8 seam, the cut far range and the softness are fixed, and almost all the specks are gone: 2 tiny marks remain on the dark ridge.

Pipeline port. A zsh runner drives one Blender session per stage, all through the slot, time-boxed and memory-checked; a full bake of the 34 objects takes about 20 minutes. Visibility is tested against the shipped meshes from the 5 plates (full resolution) and 22 engine probe views. Colour comes from the plate EXRs through a separate numpy compositor. A Metal render matches the old CPU plate on a test crop (mean |diff| 0.23 levels), so new plates could be mixed with the old ones; none were needed, because the uncovered texels are mostly smooth sky.

Root causes of the v8 defects, with evidence:
- The m8 light bake read scrambled textures: it deleted every UV layer, and the mountain, snow and scan materials sample through the active render UV.
- m8's visibility test rejected grazing surfaces and eroded creases (N.V gate plus a nearest lookup in a half-resolution map of the original geometry). At rest it drew the light bake on 93% of the shore and 37.8% of the ridge, with one global gain per object. That produced the seam and the lost base mist (defect 1).
- The specks are not cracks: 9 of 80 lie near open edges, and there are no T-junctions. They are folded or inverted scan triangles that Cycles renders two-sided but the engine culled (FrontSide), plus sub-pixel slivers that took the fill colour (defect 2). I first blamed the light bake; the first v9 build disproved that, and the log says so.
- m8 deleted faces below z -0.05 even beyond the lake, cutting 10,644 rest-visible pixels of Object_2.009/.010. The cut edge is the dark line (defect 3); it sits about 100 px left of the x the SPEC gives.
- Low texel density plus the DOF level applied as a mip bias gave 20-25% less detail on the right side (defect 4).

v9 fixes:
- Materials keep their own UVs during the light bake; only faces under the lake are deleted.
- Texel need comes from each triangle's largest screen stretch.
- Rest-first plate priority with a bilinear depth test; only the far side of depth edges is excluded; weights are feathered in UV space.
- A relaxed and a depth-matched tier on the scan mountains only.
- The fill is the plates extrapolated near plate texels, else the light bake times a spatial gain map; the gutter is dilated.
- 24.1 M texels, the plates' exact WebP encoding.
- Engine, baked path only: the DOF blur reproduced in screen space with textureGrad, and double-sided baked meshes. Each change has a URL switch back.

E-G1 at T1 with a pinned clock:
- worst region 2.0 levels (q00) and 1.3 (q03); full-frame mean |diff| 1.43 / 1.47;
- sharpness 1.00-1.08x the projected path;
- same distance to F000/F045 as the projected plates;
- strong ridge specks 8, down from 62-66 in v8.

The other gates: E-G4 passes. Environment assets are 2.05 MB. Frame time could not be measured, because the slot's background QoS throttles every build. The sky equirect and the wisp card are rendered and saved in WORK for step 2.

The press-and-hold is rebuilt as a deterministic arrangement measured from the Cycles reference. It is the new default; `?hold=r10` restores today's hold exactly.

How it works:
- Each ring follows a target pose that depends only on hold time, built in a fixed hold view frame. The press moment now only decides which identical piece goes in which slot: the code locks in a symmetry of each ring while its hold weight is exactly 0.
- Ring A makes a rigid 120-degree turn about the view axis (-1,1,-1)/sqrt3 (A2 rule R1), with fitted per-quarter push, slide, spin, roll and tilt.
- Ring B is one lid across the orb that tips over during the hold. Its halves slide along the cut, which reproduces the F358 bar growth, the F420 lid offset about 60 px left, and the seam block.
- Rings C and D swing between face-on and nearly flat on the 1.33 s beat. When flat, their walls form the lower lid of the F420 lens.
- The tumble stops while the hold controls the rings, so the release hands back to the pose the rings had at the charge's eye.
- A bounded, slow breathing motion keeps long holds alive and inside the frame.
- The hold camera move now follows the measured EXPAND_CAM/RELEASE_CAM exactly. The old springs lagged the lunge by about 0.3 s. The full-hold camera pose is unchanged, so the hold plates stay registered.

outs.summary:
The rotating hold is built and is now the default. All gates pass except perf, which could not be measured cleanly (the machine was heavily shared). I stopped my lab on :5175. MAIN's :5173 was not touched. Nothing was committed, deployed or uploaded, and no .blend file was touched.

How it works now:
- **Rings A and B:** while held, each ring keeps its own rest tumble, with the tumble clock eased down to 0.25 of rest speed. The reference turns ring A at about 0.2 of rest speed during the sustain. Because they follow the rest motion exactly, A and B cannot reverse, snap or restart.
- **Opening:** ring A's quarters and ring B's halves move outward on top of that motion. The offsets are in each ring's own frame, so the pieces keep turning with their ring. Most of the opening comes in with the camera lunge, then it grows slowly. It closes in 0.45 s after the release while the clock speeds back up to 1.
- **Rings C and D:** they do not rotate at rest (D only nods). So during a hold each gets a forward flip about the diameter it is already turning about (48 and 54 deg/s). The flip speeds up if the slowed tumble underneath works against it. After the release the flip only slows down, and it stops on a multiple of 180 deg, which looks the same as the ring's normal rest pose.
- **Removed:** the charge alignment, the pop pose, the eye and the breathing loop.
- **Kept:** fix round 1's measured camera dolly, ring A's -22.5 deg phase, and exact `?hold=r10` / `?aphase=r10`.
- **Frame guard:** each opened piece's push is limited so its silhouette stays inside the frame. It never slows or reverses the rotation.
- **Re-press:** pressing again during a release no longer cuts the release short. A click there now does nothing. A new hold starts from the current clock rate, opening and camera. Before this fix, the click window jerked ring A by +23.8 deg/s in one frame.
- **Switches:** `?hold=r11a` is the step-2 arrangement exactly as it was; `?hold=r10` is still the round-10 hold.

What I verified (live presses, every frame at 60 Hz):
- **A and B direction:** across eleven runs (holds of 1, 3, 5 (three press moments), 10 and 20 s, three re-press timings, and a click during a release), their speed relative to rest stays between 0.25 and 1 in every frame. It matches the clock rate within 0.0011 and never changes sign. The largest frame-to-frame change is 0.0253 of rest speed (A 5.84 deg/s, B 4.17 deg/s). Every A quarter and B half turns exactly with its ring.
- **C and D:** in the sustain they always turn forward (C 24 to 104 deg/s, D 27 to 76 deg/s about their flip axis). In the first second, before the clock has slowed, C's own rest nod can briefly turn against the flip (down to -77 deg/s at one press moment). After the release they go back to their rest nodding.
- **Videos:** a 10 s hold and a re-press sequence, which I reviewed as frame sheets (every 2nd to 8th frame across the whole video). No snap, no jump and no reversal of A or B.

Gates: frame bounds (H-G2), interaction (H-G3), `?hold=r10` vs MAIN (H-G4), nothing else changed (H-G5) and both typechecks pass; the numbers are in the gates list.

H-G1 (the A2 key-frame checklist) no longer applies to the default, because the user's words override the reference arrangement; it still holds for `?hold=r11a`. Against the reference sheets, the camera lunge lands at the same frames (F354-F364).

- Click is inert, no errors, typecheck 0.

- The orb has a broad lavender limb.

- perf_probe pairs (6, heavily contended): paired medians -3 / -3 / +4.5 % frame time.

That is the HOLD lane's work, not an ICE regression, and nothing in ICE interferes with it.
